items.title: BOSSAI: Inside the AI attack mesh that targeted Taiwan’s emergency services
items.summary: Acronis TRU reveals how one operator used a 12-agent AI attack mesh to target organizations across 11 countries and transform cyberthreat operations.

items.title: Configured to protect: How to properly use security policies
items.summary: Buying protection is not the same as being protected. What decides the outcome is how the protection is configured and used every day. This report looks at that gap. It uses the live configuration records behind a large managed fleet, more than 1.6 million active endpoints, to see how protection plans are actually set up, how administrators and the providers who manage them choose to structure plans and what those choices tel

items.title: Inside Qilin ransomware: ESXi attacks, affiliate networks and double extortion
items.summary: Qilin, also known as Agenda, is a Russian-speaking ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation that first appeared in 2022.

items.title: The Gentlemen: A closer look at a not-so-gentle ransomware-as-a- service operation
items.summary: The Gentlemen uses a double-extortion model. In addition to encrypting files, the ransomware can exfiltrate data from compromised systems. This puts additional pressure on victims to pay the ransom to restore access to their files and prevent the stolen data from being publicly leaked.

items.title: Acronis AI Copilot: Adoption is high and growing among MSPs
items.summary: See how users are turning to the AI assistant in Acronis Cyber Platform to get answers and complete tasks using plain-language prompts.

items.title: Acronis Cyberthreats Update, October 2026
items.summary: The Acronis Cyberthreats Update covers current cyberthreat activity and trends, as observed by Acronis Threat Research Unit (TRU) and Acronis sensors. Figures presented here were gathered in September 2026 and reflect threats that Acronis detected, as well as news stories from the industry. This report represents a global outlook and is based on more than one million unique endpoints distributed around the world.

items.title: AI agents at work: What Acronis endpoint data reveals about MSP and SMB usage
items.summary: An AI tool that produces only text carries roughly the risk of a badly worded email. A tool that can reach into systems and change things carries the risk of whatever those systems hold. The security question is not how clever the model is. It is which systems and data the model is authorized to access.

items.title: Red Heron exploits Gitea n-day flaw in multinational campaign, exposing new Linux rootkit
items.summary: Acronis Threat Research Unit (TRU) uncovered a multinational campaign in which a Chinese-speaking threat actor, tracked as Red Heron, rapidly weaponized CVE-2026-60004 to compromise internet-facing instances of Gitea, a self-hosted source-code management platform. The activity progressed from source-code theft to persistent access, credential collection, and lateral movement.

items.title: Remote access hardening playbook: Reducing RMM tool risk for SMBs
items.summary: Widely trusted tools like ConnectWise ScreenConnect and AnyDesk may be abused by attackers, and when left unattended, they can present a problem: Their legitimate prevalence makes attacker activity harder to spot, and any vulnerabilities affecting them can turn a trusted platform into an infection vector.

items.title: Cambodia-focused cluster uses multistage infection chain with localized lures
items.summary: Acronis’ Threat Research Unit (TRU) identified a recent campaign focused on Cambodia. The analyzed archives, discovered while hunting for related activity, use several lure themes, including Cambodian government notices, public health announcements, dental examination records, real estate documents, and promotional offers.

items.title: Grandoreiro goes north: From Brazil to Mexico with a new DLL sideloading campaign
items.summary: Grandoreiro is a notorious banking trojan that has been operating across Latin America since at least 2016, targeting financial institutions and their customers through phishing campaigns and social engineering techniques. Written in Delphi and Brazilian in origin, it is one of the many of Latin American banking trojans (alongside Guildma, Javali and Melcoz).

items.title: How patch quality varies by vendor across SMB Windows fleets
items.summary: Patch prioritization in SMB environments often starts with software vendor severity. Critical patches go first, then high-severity patches, then everything else. Severity answers only one question: How risky is it to leave a vulnerability unresolved? It says nothing about how hard the fix is to deploy, how often it causes issues or how much testing it needs.

items.title: PATCHCORD: New malware cluster targets Afghan telecom and South Asian critical infrastructure
items.summary: Acronis Threat Research Unit (TRU) has identified an ongoing campaign delivering a previously undocumented custom backdoor against Afghan telecom providers and South Asian critical infrastructure organizations. The backdoor, tracked as PATCHCORD, is a compiled C/C++ implant delivered through sector-specific lures, including fake VPN installers impersonating Afghan Telecom (AFTEL) and telecom management tools.

items.title: Advancing toward agent health and self-recovery for MSP operations
items.summary: The business value of better agent health assurance is straightforward. MSPs spend less time on repetitive checks and manual service recovery. Technicians can focus on issues that require judgment instead of routine restarts. Service managers can see which customers or services have repeated problems. Customers receive more stable protection and management coverage.

items.title: Two ways to scale your scripts
items.summary: Every script you run on a customer endpoint is operational software with administrator privileges. It deserves the same lifecycle discipline you would apply to any other production code — review, attribution, versioning and retirement. Whether a script was written by a senior engineer last Tuesday, cloned from a vendor template or generated by AI, the standards expectation is identical.

items.title: Lampion's Portugal-focused phishing campaign delivers multistage malware
items.summary: Acronis Threat Research Unit (TRU) has identified an active Lampion malware campaign targeting Portuguese users through phishing emails masquerading as financial and administrative communications.

items.title: Session recording adoption takes off
items.summary: Selective session recording is one of the oldest and cheapest controls in privileged-access security, and every regulatory framework that touches remote administration expects it. The control became generally available on the Acronis platform on April 22, 2026. This report measures the two months of adoption that followed, through June 23, 2026.
